Penetrating cranial gunshot injury with.normalized_text: Penetrating cranial gunshot injury with retained intracranial projectile
Penetrating cranial gunshot injury with.description: A penetrating head injury caused by a firearm projectile, with metallic foreign material retained near the skull base and associated intracranial air.

Penetrating craniofacial foreign-body in.normalized_text: Penetrating craniofacial foreign-body injury through the nasal or paranasal sinus route
Penetrating craniofacial foreign-body in.description: A foreign object can enter the cranial cavity through the nose, orbit, or paranasal sinuses and lodge near the skull base, sometimes producing pneumocephalus.

Postoperative intracranial metallic mate.normalized_text: Postoperative intracranial metallic material with postoperative pneumocephalus
Postoperative intracranial metallic mate.description: Prior neurosurgical or endovascular procedures may leave metallic clips, coils, or other devices and can cause intracranial air shortly after surgery.

Congenital aqueductal stenosis causing o.normalized_text: Congenital aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
Congenital aqueductal stenosis causing o.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct causes enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, progressive macrocephaly, and increased intracranial pressure in infancy.

Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficienc.description: A mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder in which impaired conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA produces persistent or episodic lactic acidosis, elevated pyruvate, neurologic dysfunction, and sometimes structural brain abnormalities including ventriculomegaly.

Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency.description: A severe disorder of gluconeogenesis and anaplerotic metabolism causing accumulation of pyruvate and lactate, metabolic acidosis, neurologic disease, and occasionally prenatal or infantile ventriculomegaly.

Glutaric acidemia type 1.description: An inherited lysine and tryptophan degradation disorder caused by glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. It often presents in infancy with macrocephaly, low free carnitine, episodic neurologic deterioration, and characteristic brain imaging abnormalities.

Mitochondrial disease with secondary lac.normalized_text: Mitochondrial disease with secondary lactic acidosis
Mitochondrial disease with secondary lac.description: Mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation disorders can cause recurrent metabolic decompensation, elevated lactate and pyruvate, impaired growth, secondary carnitine deficiency, and variable neurologic or structural brain abnormalities.

Primary aldosteronism (autonomous aldost.normalized_text: Primary aldosteronism (autonomous aldosterone excess, often due to an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia)
Primary aldosteronism (autonomous aldost.description: A disorder in which aldosterone production is inappropriately high relative to renin, causing suppression of renin and often hypertension with or without low potassium.

Adrenal adenoma with combined aldosteron.normalized_text: Adrenal adenoma with combined aldosterone and cortisol secretion
Adrenal adenoma with combined aldosteron.description: An adrenal cortical adenoma can occasionally co-secrete aldosterone and cortisol. This may produce biochemical evidence of primary aldosteronism along with mild autonomous cortisol secretion.

Mild autonomous cortisol secretion from.normalized_text: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion from an adrenal incidentaloma
Mild autonomous cortisol secretion from.description: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion is low-grade ACTH-independent cortisol production from an adrenal lesion, usually without obvious Cushingoid appearance. It is generally suggested by failure to suppress cortisol after dexamethasone.

ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome due to.normalized_text: ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome due to an adrenal cortisol-producing tumor
ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome due to.description: This condition results from excessive cortisol production by an adrenal adenoma or carcinoma, leading to low ACTH through negative feedback. Typical cases show persistent cortisol excess and lack of suppression with dexamethasone.

Pheochromocytoma.description: A catecholamine-secreting tumor of the adrenal medulla that may cause episodic or persistent hypertension, palpitations, headache, sweating, and anxiety.

Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial i.normalized_text: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (anterior STEMI), likely left anterior descending coronary artery occlusion
Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial i.description: An acute heart attack caused by abrupt coronary artery blockage, producing transmural ischemia/injury in the anterior and septal portions of the left ventricle.

Acute anteroseptal myocardial infarction.description: A subtype of anterior myocardial infarction affecting the interventricular septum and anterior wall, usually due to proximal or mid-left anterior descending artery occlusion.

Benign early repolarization pattern.description: A nonischemic ECG variant characterized by ST-segment elevation, most often in precordial leads, commonly seen in younger healthy individuals.

Hyperkalemia.description: Elevated serum potassium can produce ECG abnormalities including peaked T waves, PR prolongation, QRS widening, and in severe cases a sine-wave pattern.

Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvi.description: Functional obstruction of the colon causing marked colonic dilatation without an obstructing lesion, often associated with severe illness, immobility, neurologic disease, electrolyte disturbances, or medications that reduce bowel motility.

Cecal volvulus.description: Twisting of the cecum and adjacent ascending colon around its mesentery, producing a closed-loop large-bowel obstruction. The cecum may become massively dilated and displaced from its normal right-lower-quadrant location.

Mechanical large-bowel obstruction.description: Obstruction of the colon caused by a structural blockage such as colorectal cancer, diverticular stricture, fecal impaction, adhesions, or volvulus. Proximal bowel dilates with gas and fluid.

Stercoral colitis with fecal impaction.description: Inflammation and pressure injury of the colonic wall caused by impacted stool, most often in the rectosigmoid colon. It can cause obstruction, ischemia, ulceration, and perforation.

Legionario (Legionella neumonía).description: Una neumonía bacteriana atípica causada por especies de Legionella, a menudo asociada con hiponatremia, inflamación sistémica e infiltrados pulmonares de vidrio molido o nodulares en parches.

Neumonía aguda por fiebre Q (infección p.normalized_text: Neumonía aguda por fiebre Q (infección por Coxiella burnetii)
Neumonía aguda por fiebre Q (infección p.description: Una infección zoonótica endémica en algunas partes de España que puede causar neumonía atípica, hallazgos inflamatorios sistémicos y opacidades pulmonares variables en vidrio pulido o nodular.

Anaplasmosis granulocítica humana.description: Una infección transmitida por garrapatas causada por Anaplasma phagocytophilum que infecta neutrófilos; puede causar enfermedades sistémicas y, rara vez, infiltraciones pulmonares o afectación respiratoria aguda.

Leptospirosis con afectación pulmonar.description: Una infección espiroquética zoonótica que puede causar inflamación sistémica, anomalías urinarias renales, hiponatremia e infiltrados hemorrágicos pulmonares o de vidrio molido.

Bronconeumonía bacteriana aguda.description: Una infección bacteriana aguda de las respiraciones respiratorias bajas, incluyendo neumonía neumocócica u otra neumonía piogénica, que puede producir leucocitosis neutrofílica y opacidades pulmonares multifocales.

Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis.normalized_text: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis syndrome (HUVS) with renal involvement
Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis.description: A rare immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis characterized by anti-C1q antibodies, persistent hypocomplementemia, and potential glomerulonephritis, often with a membranoproliferative or crescentic pattern.

Lupus nephritis.description: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis caused by systemic lupus erythematosus, commonly associated with low complement levels, anti-C1q antibodies, hematuria, proteinuria, and progressive kidney dysfunction.

Immune-complex membranoproliferative glo.description: A glomerular injury pattern caused by immune-complex deposition and complement activation, producing mesangial proliferation, capillary-wall remodeling, hematuria, proteinuria, and hypocomplementemia.

C1q nephropathy.description: An uncommon immune-complex glomerulopathy defined by dominant C1q deposition in glomeruli, commonly presenting with proteinuria and sometimes hematuria and impaired renal function; histologic patterns may resemble focal segmental glomerulosclerosis or proliferative glomerulonephritis.

Infection-related immune-complex glomeru.description: Glomerulonephritis triggered by an active or recent infection, resulting in immune-complex deposition, complement consumption, hematuria, proteinuria, and acute or subacute kidney injury.

Clostridioides difficile infection (C. d.description: An intestinal infection caused by toxin-producing Clostridioides difficile, usually associated with diarrhea and abdominal symptoms. A positive PCR indicates presence of the organism but does not alone confirm active toxin-mediated disease.

Asymptomatic Clostridioides difficile co.description: Presence of C. difficile in the intestine without active infection or toxin-mediated colitis. PCR can remain positive in colonized individuals who do not have clinically significant diarrhea.

Leishmaniasis visceral asociada al VIH.description: Infección diseminada con parásitos Leishmania, endémicas en países mediterráneos, incluyendo España. En la infección avanzada por VIH suele causar afectación de la médula ósea, citopenias, hipergammaglobulinemia, hipoalbúminemia, hepatosplenomegalia y rara vez puede producir micronódulos pulmonares difós.

Histoplasmosis diseminada.description: Una infección sistémica por hongos causada por especies de Histoplasma que puede ocurrir en personas profundamente inmunosuprimidas con SIDA. Puede causar pancitopenia, LDH elevado, enfermedad constitucional, afectación hepatoesplénica y nódulos pulmonares miliares difusos.

Tuberculosis miliar.description: Diseminación hematógena de Mycobacterium tuberculosis produce innumerables nódulos pulmonares pequeños. La infección avanzada por VIH aumenta sustancialmente el riesgo de tuberculosis diseminada y extrapulmonar.

Infección diseminada del complejo Mycoba.normalized_text: Infección diseminada del complejo Mycobacterium avium
Infección diseminada del complejo Mycoba.description: Infección diseminada oportunista debida al complejo Mycobacterium avium, que suele ocurrir en el SIDA con recuentos de CD4 por debajo de 50/mm3. Comúnmente causa anemia, fosfatasa alcalina elevada o LDH, síntomas constitucionales, linfadenopatía y afectación hepática, bazo o médula ósea.

Neumonía por Pneumocystis jirovecii.description: Una neumonía fúngica oportunista en pacientes con VIH avanzado, especialmente cuando los recuentos de CD4 están por debajo de 200/mm3. Las imágenes clásicamente muestran infiltrados bilaterales difuntos en vidrio esmerilado o intersticiales, aunque pueden aparecer patrones nodulares atípicos.

HTLV-1-associated adult T-cell leukemia/.normalized_text: HTLV-1-associated adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) with cutaneous involvement
HTLV-1-associated adult T-cell leukemia/.description: A mature peripheral T-cell neoplasm caused by HTLV-1 infection. It can present with skin papules, plaques, nodules, erythroderma, blood abnormalities, lymphadenopathy, hypercalcemia, and systemic organ involvement.

Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymp.description: Mycosis fungoides is the most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. It usually evolves slowly from scaly patches to infiltrated plaques, papules, tumors, or erythroderma, with epidermotropic atypical T lymphocytes on biopsy.

Secondary syphilis.description: Secondary syphilis is the disseminated stage of Treponema pallidum infection and may cause a generalized papulosquamous rash, often involving the trunk, extremities, palms, and soles, with systemic symptoms and generalized lymphadenopathy.

Chronic kidney disease-associated prurit.normalized_text: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus with xerosis/uremic dermatosis
Chronic kidney disease-associated prurit.description: Advanced chronic kidney disease can cause severe xerosis, pruritus, excoriations, lichenification, pigmentary change, and scaling. Secondary hyperparathyroidism, anemia, iron dysregulation, and vitamin-D deficiency commonly accompany advanced renal failure.

Chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (Trypanoso.description: Chronic cardiac infection with Trypanosoma cruzi causing myocarditis, myocardial fibrosis, conduction-system disease, atrioventricular block, ventricular arrhythmias, heart failure, and sometimes apical aneurysm. Myocardial biopsy may show inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and intracellular amastigote nests.

Cardiac sarcoidosis.description: Granulomatous inflammatory disease involving the myocardium that can cause patchy fibrosis, atrioventricular block, ventricular tachycardia, cardiomyopathy, and sudden cardiac death. Biopsy may reveal noncaseating granulomas, although sensitivity is limited because involvement is patchy.

Giant cell myocarditis.description: A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized by myocardial destruction, inflammatory infiltrates, multinucleated giant cells, ventricular arrhythmias, high-grade heart block, and often severe ventricular dysfunction.

Postoperative wound dehiscence with surg.normalized_text: Postoperative wound dehiscence with surgical-site infection
Postoperative wound dehiscence with surg.description: Partial separation of a surgical incision, often complicated by bacterial infection and delayed wound healing.

Pyoderma gangrenosum (post-surgical pyod.description: An inflammatory neutrophilic skin disease causing rapidly progressive painful ulcers with undermined violaceous borders; it may occur at surgical sites because of pathergy.

Chronic infected wound / ulcer with bact.normalized_text: Chronic infected wound / ulcer with bacterial colonization
Chronic infected wound / ulcer with bact.description: A persistent skin ulcer in which impaired healing and bacterial colonization or infection produce exudate, slough, inflammation, and delayed closure.

Upper airway or pharyngeal foreign body.normalized_text: Upper airway or pharyngeal foreign body
Upper airway or pharyngeal foreign body.description: An inhaled or swallowed object lodged in the throat, hypopharynx, or upper airway. This may be visible on neck radiography if the object is radiopaque.

Esophageal foreign body.description: A swallowed object retained in the cervical esophagus, which can cause swallowing difficulty, throat discomfort, drooling, chest discomfort, or vomiting.

Cervical spondylosis.description: Age-related degeneration of the cervical spine involving discs, vertebral bodies, and facet joints; it may cause neck pain, stiffness, or nerve-related arm symptoms.

Giant bullous emphysema (vanishing lung.description: A severe form of bullous lung disease in which very large air-filled bullae occupy much of a hemithorax and compress remaining normal lung tissue.

Giant pulmonary bulla.description: A pulmonary bulla is a large air-containing space caused by destruction and coalescence of alveoli; a giant bulla can occupy more than one-third of a hemithorax.

Pneumothorax, possibly tension pneumotho.description: Pneumothorax is air in the pleural space causing partial or complete collapse of the lung. Tension pneumothorax produces increased intrathoracic pressure and mediastinal shift and is a medical emergency.

Congenital lobar overinflation (congenit.description: A congenital airway abnormality causing progressive overinflation of one lung lobe, sometimes presenting later in childhood or adulthood and producing compression of adjacent lung.

Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal h.normalized_text: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (PBMAH) causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome
Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal h.description: A disorder in which both adrenal glands develop nodular enlargement and autonomously produce cortisol, suppressing pituitary ACTH. It commonly presents later in adulthood and may cause mild or overt Cushing syndrome.

Bilateral cortisol-secreting adrenal ade.description: Benign adrenal adenomas can autonomously secrete cortisol. Rarely, bilateral adenomas or an adenoma with contralateral adrenal nodularity can produce ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome.

ACTH-independent adrenal Cushing syndrom.description: Cushing syndrome caused by autonomous adrenal cortisol secretion, most often from an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia. Excess cortisol suppresses ACTH and can cause metabolic and skin manifestations.

Primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical.description: A rare form of ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome caused by multiple small cortisol-producing adrenal nodules, often associated with Carney complex and more commonly diagnosed in children or young adults.

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.icd11_title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

Nephrotic syndrome.description: A renal syndrome caused by heavy urinary protein loss, leading to hypoalbuminemia, edema/anasarca, ascites, and sometimes secondary endocrine abnormalities from urinary loss of binding proteins.

Lupus nephritis due to systemic lupus er.normalized_text: Lupus nephritis due to systemic lupus erythematosus
Lupus nephritis due to systemic lupus er.description: Immune-complex kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus; it may produce proteinuria, hematuria, nephrotic syndrome, edema, and preserved creatinine early in the disease.

Minimal change disease.description: A podocyte disorder causing abrupt nephrotic syndrome, often with severe albumin loss and generalized edema while renal function remains normal or near normal.

Protein-losing enteropathy.description: Excessive gastrointestinal loss of serum proteins causing profound hypoalbuminemia, edema, ascites, and low total protein; it may be associated with autoimmune disease such as lupus.

Severe hypothyroidism with myxedema-rela.description: Deficient thyroid hormone causes fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance and edema; severe disease can contribute to serous effusions and generalized soft-tissue swelling.

Gallbladder varices due to portal hypert.normalized_text: Gallbladder varices due to portal hypertension
Gallbladder varices due to portal hypert.description: Dilated collateral veins within or around the gallbladder wall caused by elevated portal venous pressure, often associated with portal vein obstruction or cavernous transformation.

Chronic portal vein thrombosis with cave.normalized_text: Chronic portal vein thrombosis with cavernous transformation
Chronic portal vein thrombosis with cave.description: Long-standing portal vein obstruction can lead to formation of numerous periportal collateral veins (portal cavernoma), portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and gallbladder wall varices.

Portal hypertensive cholecystopathy.description: Gallbladder wall edema and/or varices occurring as a manifestation of portal hypertension, typically in patients with cirrhosis or extrahepatic portal venous obstruction.

Polyarteritis nodosa.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause multiple visceral arterial microaneurysms, stenoses, thrombosis, and renal infarction while usually sparing glomerular capillaries.

Segmental arterial mediolysis.description: A noninflammatory arteriopathy causing degeneration of the arterial media, with dissections, aneurysms, stenoses, and infarction, most often affecting abdominal visceral arteries.

Fibromuscular dysplasia.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory disorder of medium-sized arteries, commonly renal and carotid arteries, producing alternating stenosis and dilatation (a string-of-beads appearance), aneurysms, dissections, or renal infarcts.

Systemic vasculitis with renal medium-ve.normalized_text: Systemic vasculitis with renal medium-vessel involvement, such as ANCA-associated vasculitis
Systemic vasculitis with renal medium-ve.description: Systemic inflammatory vasculitides can cause renal vascular injury and ischemia, although small-vessel glomerulonephritis is generally more characteristic of ANCA-associated disease than multiple medium-vessel aneurysms.

Tuberculous aortitis with infected abdom.normalized_text: Tuberculous aortitis with infected abdominal aortic aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm
Tuberculous aortitis with infected abdom.description: Rare extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving the aortic wall, causing inflammatory destruction, pseudoaneurysm or aneurysm formation, and sometimes fistulization into adjacent bowel or retroperitoneal structures.

Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary.normalized_text: Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and vascular involvement
Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary.description: Disseminated tuberculosis is infection affecting multiple organs outside the lungs, potentially including bowel, lymph nodes, kidneys, vascular structures, and the aorta. Gastrointestinal tuberculosis often involves the ileocecal region and may produce ulceration.

Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (myco.normalized_text: Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (mycotic aneurysm), possibly due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (myco.description: A mycotic aneurysm is an infected arterial aneurysm caused by microbial invasion of the vessel wall. It commonly causes rapid aneurysm expansion, periaortic inflammation, systemic inflammatory markers, anemia, and risk of rupture or fistula formation.

Aortoenteric fistula secondary to inflam.normalized_text: Aortoenteric fistula secondary to inflammatory or infected abdominal aortic aneurysm
Aortoenteric fistula secondary to inflam.description: An aortoenteric fistula is an abnormal communication between the aorta and gastrointestinal tract, usually associated with an aortic aneurysm, graft infection, or severe adjacent inflammation. It can cause occult or overt gastrointestinal bleeding, anemia, infection, and bowel ulceration.

Focal hepatic brucellosis (brucellar hep.normalized_text: Focal hepatic brucellosis (brucellar hepatic abscess/brucelloma) with erythema nodosum
Focal hepatic brucellosis (brucellar hep.description: A localized hepatic manifestation of Brucella infection, often occurring in Mediterranean regions such as Spain. It can produce a granulomatous liver mass or abscess and may be accompanied by immune-mediated skin findings including erythema nodosum.

Hepatic tuberculosis with erythema nodos.description: Tuberculosis can cause granulomatous inflammation and focal hepatic lesions or abscess-like masses. Erythema nodosum can occur as a hypersensitivity reaction to tuberculosis.

Hepatosplenic cat-scratch disease (Barto.description: Systemic Bartonella henselae infection can cause hepatic or splenic granulomatous lesions in immunocompetent patients and may be associated with erythema nodosum or other inflammatory skin eruptions.

Intracranial dural arteriovenous fistula.description: An abnormal direct connection between meningeal arteries and dural venous sinuses or cortical veins, which can cause venous congestion and prominent tortuous intracranial vessels.

Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with co.normalized_text: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with collateral venous circulation
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with co.description: Thrombosis of a dural venous sinus can obstruct cerebral venous drainage and lead to enlarged collateral cortical and extracranial veins, venous congestion, and sometimes hemorrhagic infarction.

Cerebral arteriovenous malformation.description: A congenital vascular malformation consisting of abnormal high-flow connections between arteries and veins, often producing a tangle of enlarged vessels and early venous drainage.

Hepatic hemangioma.description: A benign vascular liver tumor, often incidentally detected. On contrast CT it commonly shows peripheral nodular enhancement with progressive centripetal fill-in; large lesions may be heterogeneous.

Focal nodular hyperplasia.description: A benign hyperplastic liver lesion composed of normal hepatocytes and abnormal vessels. It is usually asymptomatic and may show strong arterial enhancement with a central scar and delayed scar enhancement.

Hepatocellular adenoma.description: A benign hepatocellular tumor that may occur in people with hormonal exposure, obesity, metabolic disease, or anabolic steroid use. It can be hypervascular and may hemorrhage or undergo malignant transformation in selected subtypes.

Hepatic metastases from a hypervascular.normalized_text: Hepatic metastases from a hypervascular primary tumor
Hepatic metastases from a hypervascular.description: Metastatic liver disease occurs when a malignancy from another organ spreads to the liver. Hypervascular metastases may arise from neuroendocrine tumors, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, or some other primary cancers.

Acromegaly.description: A disorder caused by excess growth hormone, usually from a pituitary adenoma, producing progressive enlargement of the hands, feet, facial bones, and soft tissues.

Pachydermoperiostosis (primary hypertrop.description: A rare genetic condition characterized by clubbing of the fingers and toes, thickened skin, enlargement of distal extremities, and periosteal new bone formation.

Chronic lymphedema with elephantiasis.description: Persistent failure of lymphatic drainage causing progressive swelling, skin thickening, fibrosis, recurrent inflammation, and deformity of an affected limb or foot.

Chronic tophaceous gout.description: A disorder of monosodium urate crystal deposition that can cause recurrent inflammatory arthritis, destructive joint deformity, and firm tophi around joints, toes, fingers, and nail areas.

Psoriatic arthritis with dactylitis.description: An inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis that may cause swollen 'sausage' digits, joint damage, nail abnormalities, and deformity of hands and feet.

Type 2 Brugada electrocardiographic patt.description: A saddleback ST-segment elevation pattern in the right precordial leads, usually V1-V2, which can suggest Brugada syndrome but is not diagnostic without a type 1 pattern and appropriate clinical context.

Brugada syndrome.description: An inherited cardiac sodium-channel disorder that predisposes to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Diagnosis generally requires a spontaneous or provoked type 1 Brugada ECG pattern plus supportive clinical evaluation.

Incomplete right bundle branch block.description: A conduction delay through the right bundle branch that may produce an rSr' or rsR' pattern in V1-V2 with a narrow or mildly prolonged QRS duration. It is often benign but can resemble Brugada-pattern ECG changes.

Early repolarization pattern.description: A usually benign ECG variant characterized by J-point elevation and mild concave ST-segment elevation, commonly seen in healthy individuals and sometimes extending into precordial leads.

HIV/AIDS with Pneumocystis jirovecii pne.normalized_text: HIV/AIDS with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cerebral toxoplasmosis
HIV/AIDS with Pneumocystis jirovecii pne.description: Advanced HIV infection can cause simultaneous opportunistic infections, including diffuse Pneumocystis pneumonia in the lungs and multifocal toxoplasmosis lesions in the brain.

Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary.normalized_text: Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary and central nervous system involvement
Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary.description: Tuberculosis can disseminate from the lungs to the brain, producing pulmonary nodules or infiltrates and intracranial tuberculomas or meningitis.

Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmona.normalized_text: Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmonary cryptococcosis and cryptococcal CNS disease
Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmona.description: Cryptococcus is an opportunistic fungal infection that may involve the lungs and central nervous system, particularly in people with advanced immunosuppression.

Pulmonary nocardiosis with disseminated.normalized_text: Pulmonary nocardiosis with disseminated nocardial brain abscesses
Pulmonary nocardiosis with disseminated.description: Nocardia can cause lung infection followed by hematogenous spread to the brain, where it may produce multiple abscesses; it is more common in immunocompromised patients.

Neurosarcoidosis with pulmonary sarcoido.description: Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease that commonly affects the lungs and can less commonly affect the central nervous system.

Deep infiltrating intestinal endometrios.normalized_text: Deep infiltrating intestinal endometriosis with ureteral involvement
Deep infiltrating intestinal endometrios.description: Endometriosis is the presence of endometrial-type glands and stroma outside the uterus. Deep infiltrating disease can involve the bowel wall and ureter, producing inflammatory masses, bowel narrowing, and urinary obstruction.

Colorectal adenocarcinoma.description: Colorectal adenocarcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumor of the colon or rectum that may form an ulcerated, infiltrative mass causing progressive bowel obstruction.

Crohn disease involving the colon or dis.normalized_text: Crohn disease involving the colon or distal small bowel
Crohn disease involving the colon or dis.description: Crohn disease is a chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can cause ulcers, inflammatory masses, fibrosis, and strictures anywhere in the gastrointestinal tract.

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma of gastric origin
diagnoses.normalized_text: Poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma of gastric origin

Trousseau syndrome due to gastric adenoc.normalized_text: Trousseau syndrome due to gastric adenocarcinoma
Trousseau syndrome due to gastric adenoc.description: Cancer-associated hypercoagulability causing recurrent arterial or venous thrombosis, often associated with advanced mucin-producing adenocarcinomas such as gastric cancer.

Gastric adenocarcinoma.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the stomach that may form an ulcerated or infiltrative mass and can metastasize or induce a hypercoagulable state.

Acute limb ischemia from arterial thromb.normalized_text: Acute limb ischemia from arterial thromboembolism
Acute limb ischemia from arterial thromb.description: Abrupt reduction in arterial blood flow to a limb, caused by embolus or in-situ thrombosis, resulting in threatened tissue viability and possible gangrene.

Disseminated intravascular coagulation a.normalized_text: Disseminated intravascular coagulation associated with malignancy
Disseminated intravascular coagulation a.description: A systemic coagulation disorder in which widespread activation of clotting causes microvascular thrombosis and may also lead to bleeding; advanced adenocarcinoma can be an underlying cause.

Prostatic malakoplakia.description: A rare chronic granulomatous inflammatory disorder, usually affecting the genitourinary tract. It is characterized histologically by macrophages containing Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and can produce FDG-avid masses that mimic cancer.

Prostate adenocarcinoma.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the prostate, commonly detected through elevated PSA, abnormal prostate examination, biopsy, or imaging. It may show focal uptake on PET imaging depending on the tracer used.

Chronic bacterial prostatitis.description: Persistent inflammation of the prostate, often associated with recurrent bacterial urinary infection, pelvic discomfort, urinary symptoms, and inflammatory changes on pathology.

Meigs syndrome.description: A rare benign syndrome consisting of an ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma associated with ascites and pleural effusion, usually right-sided; the fluid typically resolves after removal of the ovarian tumor.

Pseudo-Meigs syndrome.description: Ascites and pleural effusion occurring with a pelvic tumor other than an ovarian fibroma, including benign ovarian tumors, uterine leiomyomas, or metastatic pelvic malignancies.

Epithelial ovarian cancer with malignant.normalized_text: Epithelial ovarian cancer with malignant ascites and pleural effusion
Epithelial ovarian cancer with malignant.description: Ovarian carcinoma can spread within the peritoneal cavity and pleural space, producing a pelvic mass, ascites, pleural effusion, and increased FDG uptake on PET.

Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma without.normalized_text: Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma without confirmed Meigs syndrome
Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma without.description: A usually benign sex-cord stromal ovarian tumor that is often solid and may be associated with ascites; when ascites and pleural effusion coexist, it is termed Meigs syndrome.

Cervical tuberculous spondylitis (Pott d.normalized_text: Cervical tuberculous spondylitis (Pott disease) with prevertebral/retropharyngeal abscess
Cervical tuberculous spondylitis (Pott d.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the cervical vertebrae and intervertebral discs, often causing vertebral destruction and a large prevertebral or retropharyngeal abscess. Cervical involvement is less common than thoracic or lumbar disease but can threaten the airway or spinal cord.

Brucellar cervical spondylodiscitis.description: Brucellosis is a zoonotic bacterial infection that can involve the spine, producing spondylodiscitis, vertebral marrow inflammation, and occasionally paravertebral or epidural inflammatory collections. It is particularly relevant in Mediterranean countries including Spain.

Pyogenic cervical spondylodiscitis with.normalized_text: Pyogenic cervical spondylodiscitis with prevertebral abscess
Pyogenic cervical spondylodiscitis with.description: Bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. It may spread into the prevertebral, retropharyngeal, or epidural spaces and can cause neurologic compromise.

Cervical vertebral osteomyelitis due to.normalized_text: Cervical vertebral osteomyelitis due to fungal infection or another atypical organism
Cervical vertebral osteomyelitis due to.description: Less common infectious causes of vertebral osteomyelitis, including fungal infections or atypical bacteria, can cause chronic vertebral destruction and paraspinal soft-tissue collections, especially in immunocompromised patients.

Connective tissue nevus (collagenoma, in.normalized_text: Connective tissue nevus (collagenoma, including a shagreen patch)
Connective tissue nevus (collagenoma, in.description: A benign hamartoma with excess dermal collagen, often presenting as a skin-colored, thickened, irregular plaque on the lower back or lumbosacral region. A shagreen patch is a collagenoma classically associated with tuberous sclerosis complex.

Morphea (localized scleroderma), deep or.description: An autoimmune localized fibrosing skin disorder causing indurated plaques and, in deeper forms, involvement of the subcutaneous tissue, fascia, or muscle.

Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.description: A slow-growing, locally infiltrative dermal spindle-cell tumor that commonly presents on the trunk as a firm plaque or nodular lesion and can extend into subcutaneous tissue.

Nevus lipomatosus superficialis.description: A benign cutaneous hamartoma characterized by ectopic mature adipose tissue in the dermis, usually presenting as grouped soft papules or plaques on the lower trunk, buttocks, or pelvic region.

Cystic fibrosis with bronchiectasis.description: An inherited CFTR disorder causing thick airway secretions, recurrent infection, mucus impaction, and progressive bronchiectasis, often most marked in the upper lobes.

Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis.description: A hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus, usually in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, producing central bronchiectasis, mucus impaction, and recurrent pulmonary infiltrates.

Nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary d.description: Chronic lung infection caused by environmental mycobacteria, such as Mycobacterium avium complex, which can cause bronchiectasis, bronchiolitis, nodules, scarring, and occasionally cavitary upper-lobe disease.

Post-tuberculous bronchiectasis.description: Permanent airway dilation and fibrosis occurring after prior pulmonary tuberculosis, commonly involving upper lobes and sometimes associated with volume loss, scarring, calcification, or cavitation.

Invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast.normalized_text: Invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast
Invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast.description: The most common type of invasive breast cancer, arising from breast ducts and infiltrating surrounding tissue. It often appears as an irregular mass on ultrasound and as an enhancing lesion on contrast-enhanced MRI.

Invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast.normalized_text: Invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast
Invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast.description: An invasive breast malignancy originating in lobules. It can be difficult to detect on mammography in dense breasts and may present on MRI as an irregular enhancing mass or non-mass enhancement.

High-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with.normalized_text: High-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with invasive component
High-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with.description: Ductal carcinoma in situ is a noninvasive malignant proliferation within breast ducts; extensive or high-grade disease may coexist with invasive carcinoma and can enhance on MRI.

Phyllodes tumor.description: A fibroepithelial breast tumor that may be benign, borderline, or malignant. It can grow into a large mass and often appears as a solid hypoechoic lesion on ultrasound.

Birdshot chorioretinopathy.description: A chronic bilateral posterior uveitis, strongly associated with HLA-A29, characterized by choroidal inflammatory lesions, retinal vasculitis, optic-disc leakage, and progressive visual-field loss.

Sarcoid posterior uveitis.description: Ocular sarcoidosis can cause bilateral granulomatous uveitis, retinal periphlebitis, optic-disc inflammation, chorioretinal lesions, and visual-field abnormalities.

Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease.description: A bilateral autoimmune panuveitis affecting melanocyte-containing tissues, usually producing diffuse choroidal inflammation, optic-disc hyperfluorescence, serous retinal detachments, and visual impairment.

Autoimmune retinopathy, including cancer.description: An immune-mediated retinal degeneration that can produce bilateral photoreceptor dysfunction, ring scotomas, retinal vascular attenuation, and relatively subtle early fundus changes.

Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy (AZ.description: An outer-retinal inflammatory disorder causing acute or progressive zonal visual-field defects, often with minimal early fundus changes and later retinal pigment epithelial alterations.

Classical Hodgkin lymphoma.description: A B-cell lymphoma characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory cellular background. The tumor cells typically express CD30 and CD15.

Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymp.description: A subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma with scattered Reed-Sternberg cells in a prominent mixed inflammatory background, often including lymphocytes, eosinophils, histiocytes, and plasma cells. Reed-Sternberg cells are usually CD30-positive and CD15-positive.

Nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymp.description: The most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma, usually involving mediastinal lymph nodes and characterized by fibrous bands and lacunar-type Reed-Sternberg cells. The malignant cells generally express CD30 and often CD15.

Anaplastic large cell lymphoma.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that can contain large pleomorphic cells and may mimic classical Hodgkin lymphoma. It is usually distinguished by T-cell-marker expression, ALK testing, EMA expression, and lack of the typical classical Hodgkin lymphoma immunophenotype.

Intralobar pulmonary sequestration.description: A congenital abnormal segment of lung, usually in a lower lobe, that receives systemic arterial blood supply from the aorta rather than the pulmonary circulation. It may appear as a mass and can become infected or inflamed.

Bronchial carcinoid tumor.description: A usually slow-growing neuroendocrine lung tumor that can be highly vascular and may arise centrally or peripherally. It can demonstrate uptake on functional imaging and may be associated with hilar lymph-node involvement.

Primary lung cancer with hilar/mediastin.normalized_text: Primary lung cancer with hilar/mediastinal lymph-node metastases
Primary lung cancer with hilar/mediastin.description: A malignant pulmonary neoplasm, such as non-small-cell lung cancer, that may present as a lung mass with FDG-avid hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes on PET/CT.

Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation.description: An abnormal direct connection between a pulmonary artery and vein, producing a vascular lung lesion that may be visible on angiography. It is sometimes associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

Helicobacter pylori-associated chronic a.description: Chronic inflammation of the gastric mucosa caused by Helicobacter pylori infection, typically showing lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, neutrophilic activity, and organisms along the surface mucus layer or gastric pits. The immunostain appears to highlight curved bacterial organisms consistent with H. pylori.

Chronic gastritis, nonspecific.description: Persistent inflammation of the stomach lining characterized histologically by lymphocytes and plasma cells in the lamina propria. It may result from H. pylori, autoimmune disease, medications, bile reflux, or other causes.

Autoimmune metaplastic atrophic gastriti.description: Immune-mediated chronic gastritis that predominantly affects the gastric body and fundus, causing oxyntic gland loss, atrophy, intestinal or pseudopyloric metaplasia, and possible vitamin B12 deficiency.

Microscopic hematuria aislada.description: Presencia de una pequeña cantidad de sangre en la orina detectable solo mediante tira reactiva, sin otros hallazgos urinarios evidentes. Puede ser transitoria o requerir confirmación con sedimento urinario.

Hematuria transitoria por ejercicio físi.normalized_text: Hematuria transitoria por ejercicio físico, traumatismo leve o deshidratación
Hematuria transitoria por ejercicio físi.description: La actividad física intensa, pequeños traumatismos o cambios transitorios en la hidratación pueden producir sangre microscópica temporal en la orina sin infección ni daño renal persistente.

Contaminación de la muestra por menstrua.normalized_text: Contaminación de la muestra por menstruación o sangrado genital
Contaminación de la muestra por menstrua.description: La sangre procedente de menstruación, sangrado vaginal u otra fuente genital puede contaminar una muestra de orina y causar un resultado de sangre en trazas.

Litiasis urinaria o renal.description: Los cálculos en riñón, uréter o vejiga pueden irritar el tracto urinario y producir hematuria microscópica o visible.

Infección urinaria baja.description: Infección de vejiga o uretra que puede ocasionar sangre en la orina, ardor al orinar, aumento de la frecuencia urinaria y urgencia miccional.

Enfermedad glomerular o renal.description: Algunas enfermedades de los glomérulos renales pueden causar hematuria microscópica, con frecuencia acompañada de proteínas en orina, hipertensión, edema o alteración de la función renal.

Congenital dysfibrinogenemia.description: An inherited qualitative fibrinogen disorder caused by variants in fibrinogen genes such as FGA, FGB, or FGG. Fibrinogen may be present but function abnormally, causing reduced functional fibrinogen assay results and variable risks of bleeding or thrombosis.

Congenital hypodysfibrinogenemia.description: A hereditary disorder in which fibrinogen is both quantitatively reduced and functionally abnormal. It is commonly associated with heterozygous variants in fibrinogen-chain genes and can produce discordance among fibrinogen/clotting assays.

Hereditary fibrinogen gamma-chain (FGG).description: An inherited fibrinogen disorder caused specifically by an FGG gene variant. Gamma-chain abnormalities can impair fibrin polymerization, alter functional fibrinogen testing, and occasionally increase thrombosis risk depending on the variant.

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the lung
diagnoses.normalized_text: Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the lung

Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphom.description: An aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma arising in the anterior mediastinum, often producing a bulky mediastinal mass with compression or invasion of adjacent structures.

Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular scle.normalized_text: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis type
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular scle.description: A lymphoma that commonly presents with a bulky mediastinal mass, especially in the nodular sclerosis subtype, and may cause systemic inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.

Anaplastic large cell lymphoma.description: A T-cell lymphoma composed of large pleomorphic cells that may have irregular or kidney-shaped nuclei; it can involve mediastinal lymph nodes and extranodal sites and is strongly FDG-avid.

Mediastinal tuberculosis with tuberculou.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy or mediastinal inflammatory masses, sometimes eroding into or compressing the esophagus.

Descending necrotizing mediastinitis or.normalized_text: Descending necrotizing mediastinitis or mediastinal abscess
Descending necrotizing mediastinitis or.description: A severe bacterial infection of mediastinal soft tissues, often arising from an oropharyngeal, dental, cervical, or esophageal source, that can produce mediastinal collections and systemic inflammation.

Noonan syndrome (RASopathy-associated T-.description: A genetic RAS/MAPK-pathway disorder characterized by distinctive facial features, webbed or broad neck, chest abnormalities, congenital heart disease, short stature, and occasionally neonatal or transient immune abnormalities including T-cell lymphopenia.

22q11.2 deletion syndrome (DiGeorge synd.description: A chromosomal deletion disorder that can cause thymic hypoplasia, neonatal T-cell lymphopenia, reduced naive T cells, congenital cardiac defects, palatal abnormalities, hypocalcemia, and characteristic facial features. Immune severity ranges from mild to severe and may improve with age.

CHARGE syndrome.description: A multisystem developmental disorder, usually caused by CHD7 variants, characterized by coloboma, heart defects, choanal atresia, growth/developmental delay, genital abnormalities, ear anomalies, and variable thymic hypoplasia causing T-cell lymphopenia.

Kabuki syndrome.description: A genetic developmental syndrome, usually due to KMT2D or KDM6A variants, with distinctive facial features, developmental delay, skeletal abnormalities, persistent fetal fingertip pads, and variable immune dysfunction including antibody deficiency, elevated IgE, and sometimes T-cell abnormalities.

Human intestinal spirochetosis.description: Colonization or infection of the colonic mucosal surface by Brachyspira species, commonly Brachyspira aalborgi or Brachyspira pilosicoli. Histology classically shows a dense basophilic fringe along the epithelial surface, representing adherent spirochetes.

Inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative c.normalized_text: Inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis or Crohn colitis)
Inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative c.description: Chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract that may cause colonic erythema, friability, erosions, and inflammatory infiltrates on biopsy.

Infectious colitis due to another bacter.normalized_text: Infectious colitis due to another bacterial pathogen
Infectious colitis due to another bacter.description: Acute bacterial infections of the colon, such as Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, or pathogenic Escherichia coli, can produce mucosal inflammation and diarrhea.

Acute pulmonary embolism.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial branches by thrombus, usually originating from deep venous thrombosis in the pelvis or lower extremities.

Pelvic deep venous thrombosis.description: Thrombus formation in pelvic veins, such as the iliac, internal iliac, or gonadal/ovarian veins; it can embolize to the lungs.

Ovarian vein thrombosis.description: Thrombosis of an ovarian (gonadal) vein, most often associated with pregnancy, postpartum status, pelvic infection, surgery, malignancy, or hypercoagulable states; pulmonary embolism can occur.

Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), lik.normalized_text: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), likely CYBB-related X-linked CGD
Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), lik.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by impaired NADPH oxidase activity in phagocytes, resulting in defective oxidative burst and susceptibility to severe infections with catalase-positive bacteria and fungi. The rhodamine/DHR flow-cytometry pattern and sequencing image support an oxidative-burst defect with a possible CYBB gene variant.

X-linked CGD carrier state with skewed X.normalized_text: X-linked CGD carrier state with skewed X-chromosome inactivation
X-linked CGD carrier state with skewed X.description: Females heterozygous for a CYBB mutation can have two neutrophil populations on DHR testing. If X-chromosome inactivation is markedly skewed, the proportion of functionally defective neutrophils may be high enough to cause clinically significant CGD-like infections.

Severe bacterial pneumonia with parapneu.normalized_text: Severe bacterial pneumonia with parapneumonic pleural effusions
Severe bacterial pneumonia with parapneu.description: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma, commonly bacterial, that may produce lobar or multilobar consolidation and reactive or infected pleural fluid collections.

Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.description: A primary liver cancer arising from intrahepatic bile duct epithelial cells, typically forming glandular tumor structures within a dense fibrous/desmoplastic stroma. It may present as one or more hepatic masses with diffusion restriction and delayed enhancement on MRI.

Hepatic metastases from adenocarcinoma.description: Secondary liver involvement by an adenocarcinoma from another primary site, commonly colorectal, pancreaticobiliary, gastric, breast, or lung cancer. Metastatic adenocarcinomas can produce multiple liver lesions and glandular malignant histology with desmoplastic fibrosis.

Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcino.description: A rare primary hepatic malignancy with both hepatocellular and biliary epithelial differentiation. Imaging can be heterogeneous and may resemble cholangiocarcinoma or metastatic disease; pathology may demonstrate glandular biliary-type malignant components with fibrosis.

Parapharyngeal schwannoma.description: A benign, encapsulated peripheral-nerve-sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells. In the parapharyngeal space it may arise from the vagus nerve, sympathetic chain, or other cranial/cervical nerves.

Cellular schwannoma.description: A histologic variant of schwannoma characterized by a highly cellular spindle-cell appearance, often with less obvious Antoni A/Antoni B zoning and fewer Verocay bodies than conventional schwannoma.

Neurofibroma.description: A benign peripheral-nerve-sheath tumor containing Schwann cells, fibroblasts, and other neural elements. Solitary neurofibromas can occur in the head and neck but are usually less encapsulated than schwannomas.

Cerebral small-vessel disease (chronic m.normalized_text: Cerebral small-vessel disease (chronic microangiopathic white-matter disease)
Cerebral small-vessel disease (chronic m.description: Chronic injury to deep and periventricular white matter caused by disease of small cerebral blood vessels, often associated with aging, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or other vascular risk factors.

Multiple sclerosis.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that commonly produces multifocal lesions in periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal-cord white matter.

Adult-onset leukodystrophy or inherited.description: A group of genetic disorders causing progressive dysfunction or loss of cerebral white matter; MRI often shows bilateral, symmetric, confluent white-matter abnormalities.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopat.description: A JC-virus infection of the brain in immunosuppressed individuals that causes progressive demyelination, usually with multifocal white-matter lesions.

diagnoses.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
diagnoses.icd11_title: Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx[Bilateral]

Mucosal leishmaniasis.description: A chronic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania species that can involve the nasal, nasopharyngeal, oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal mucosa. It may cause destructive nasal lesions and inflammatory laryngeal disease.

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis.description: A systemic small-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the upper respiratory tract and can produce chronic nasal inflammation, crusting, septal perforation, and subglottic or laryngeal stenosis.

Cocaine-induced midline destructive lesi.description: Chronic intranasal cocaine exposure can cause ischemic injury, crusting, chronic rhinitis, septal perforation, and destruction of nasal midline structures. Extension to the pharynx or larynx is less typical.

Rhinoscleroma.description: A chronic granulomatous bacterial infection caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis that affects the nose and can extend to the nasopharynx, pharynx, and larynx, producing obstructive inflammatory masses and scarring.

Cervical tuberculous lymphadenitis (scro.normalized_text: Cervical tuberculous lymphadenitis (scrofula) with a draining sinus
Cervical tuberculous lymphadenitis (scro.description: Tuberculosis involving cervical lymph nodes can form chronic painless neck masses, liquefy into a cold abscess, calcify, and eventually drain through the skin.

Cervicofacial actinomycosis.description: A chronic bacterial infection caused by Actinomyces species that produces indurated cervicofacial masses, abscesses, and draining cutaneous sinus tracts; it may follow dental disease or oral trauma.

Infected thyroglossal duct cyst.description: A congenital midline neck cyst arising from persistence of the thyroglossal duct. It can become infected, enlarge, form an abscess, and occasionally drain through the skin.

Thyroid carcinoma with cervical lymph-no.normalized_text: Thyroid carcinoma with cervical lymph-node metastasis or skin invasion
Thyroid carcinoma with cervical lymph-no.description: Thyroid malignancy, particularly papillary thyroid carcinoma, may present as a thyroid or cervical nodal mass and can contain calcifications. Advanced tumors can invade surrounding tissues and rarely ulcerate through skin.

Cervical hydatid cyst (echinococcosis).description: Hydatid disease caused by Echinococcus can rarely affect the neck or thyroid. It may produce a slowly enlarging mass and can show wall calcification; Spain is an area where echinococcosis can occur.

Erythema marginatum (classically associa.normalized_text: Erythema marginatum (classically associated with acute rheumatic fever)
Erythema marginatum (classically associa.description: A transient, nonpruritic, pink-to-red annular or serpiginous rash with central clearing, usually affecting the trunk and proximal limbs. It is a major skin manifestation of acute rheumatic fever.

Acute urticaria (hives).description: A common hypersensitivity skin eruption characterized by transient erythematous wheals that may coalesce into large annular or polycyclic plaques. It may be triggered by infection, medication, foods, or physical stimuli.

Erythema annulare centrifugum.description: A reactive annular erythema in which lesions slowly expand outward with central clearing, sometimes associated with infections, medications, or other immune triggers. The superficial form often has a trailing scale.

Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis.normalized_text: Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis
Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis.description: An expanding red annular rash caused by Borrelia infection after a tick bite. It may develop central clearing and can be multiple when infection is disseminated.

Rapunzel syndrome (gastric trichobezoar.normalized_text: Rapunzel syndrome (gastric trichobezoar with intestinal extension)
Rapunzel syndrome (gastric trichobezoar.description: A large mass of ingested hair (trichobezoar) occupying the stomach and extending through the pylorus into the small intestine. The endoscopic images show a hair-containing gastric mass, and CT shows an intragastric mottled mass with an intestinal tail.

Gastric trichobezoar without clinically.normalized_text: Gastric trichobezoar without clinically specified Rapunzel syndrome
Gastric trichobezoar without clinically.description: A compact accumulation of swallowed hair in the stomach, usually causing a molded intragastric mass. It may cause gastric obstruction, ulceration, anemia, or secondary inflammation.

Gastric phytobezoar.description: An intragastric mass of undigested vegetable or fruit fibers, often occurring with impaired gastric motility, prior gastric surgery, or excessive intake of high-fiber foods. It can resemble a bezoar on CT but does not usually contain hair.

Intestinal tuberculosis.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the gastrointestinal tract, usually causing granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis. Acid-fast bacilli may be demonstrable on Ziehl-Neelsen staining.

Gastrointestinal infection due to nontub.normalized_text: Gastrointestinal infection due to nontuberculous mycobacteria
Gastrointestinal infection due to nontub.description: Infection of the bowel or other tissues by mycobacteria other than M. tuberculosis, such as Mycobacterium avium complex. It may produce granulomatous or histiocytic inflammation and acid-fast organisms, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

Crohn disease.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can cause transmural intestinal inflammation and noncaseating granulomas, often involving the terminal ileum and colon.

Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), poss.normalized_text: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), possibly related to hypertension
Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), poss.description: Thickening of the left ventricular heart muscle, often caused by longstanding high blood pressure or other conditions that increase cardiac workload. The ECG shows high QRS voltage compatible with LVH.

Hypertensive heart disease.description: Structural and functional heart changes caused by chronic arterial hypertension, commonly including left ventricular hypertrophy and later diastolic dysfunction.

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.description: A usually inherited condition characterized by abnormal thickening of the heart muscle, often involving the interventricular septum. It can produce high ECG voltage and repolarization abnormalities.

Normal sinus rhythm with benign high QRS.normalized_text: Normal sinus rhythm with benign high QRS voltage
Normal sinus rhythm with benign high QRS.description: Some individuals, particularly younger or thin patients and athletes, can have high-voltage ECG complexes without structural heart disease. The tracing appears to show a regular sinus rhythm.

Tracheal diverticulum (paratracheal air.description: A small air-filled outpouching arising from the tracheal wall, most often located at the right posterolateral upper thoracic trachea. It is commonly an incidental congenital or acquired finding.

Tracheal bronchus.description: A congenital anatomic variant in which an accessory bronchus arises directly from the trachea, usually on the right side and often supplying the right upper lobe. It may be asymptomatic or predispose to recurrent infection.

Pneumomediastinum.description: Free air within the mediastinum, typically caused by alveolar rupture, trauma, vomiting, severe coughing, or esophageal injury. CT usually shows linear or loculated mediastinal air around the trachea and vessels.

Erythema migrans (Lyme disease).description: An expanding red skin lesion caused by Borrelia infection after an Ixodes tick bite. It may form an annular or target-like rash and can occur without fever or other systemic symptoms.

Tinea corporis (ringworm).description: A superficial fungal skin infection that produces a round or ring-shaped red rash, often with a more active outer border and central clearing.

Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis.description: Skin inflammation caused by contact with an allergen or irritant, such as adhesive, clothing, topical products, plants, or chemicals. It can cause localized redness with sharply defined borders.

Fixed drug eruption.description: A localized medication-related skin reaction that often appears as a sharply defined red, dusky, or violaceous patch and may recur in the same location after taking a medication.

Arthropod bite reaction.description: A localized inflammatory reaction after a bite from a tick, mosquito, spider, or other arthropod. Reactions may cause redness, swelling, itching, and occasionally a target-like pattern.

Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (.description: A nontraumatic tear or intramural hematoma within a coronary artery wall that narrows the true lumen and can cause acute coronary syndrome, often without major atherosclerotic plaque.

Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome.description: Myocardial ischemia caused by reduced coronary blood flow without persistent ST-segment elevation; it may result from plaque disruption, coronary dissection, spasm, or other coronary obstruction.

Vasospastic angina (coronary artery spas.description: Transient constriction of an epicardial coronary artery that produces myocardial ischemia, often with reversible angiographic narrowing and transient ECG changes.

Obstructive coronary artery disease due.normalized_text: Obstructive coronary artery disease due to atherosclerotic plaque
Obstructive coronary artery disease due.description: Coronary narrowing caused by cholesterol-rich plaque accumulation, which can impair myocardial blood flow or lead to acute plaque rupture and myocardial infarction.

Ectrodactyly-ectodermal dysplasia-clefti.description: A genetic TP63-associated disorder characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations, ectodermal abnormalities such as missing teeth, and sometimes cleft lip or palate.

Split-hand/split-foot malformation with.description: A congenital limb-malformation spectrum involving ectrodactyly or split-hand/split-foot deformities, sometimes associated with tibial or other long-bone defects.

TP63-related ankyloblepharon-ectodermal.description: A TP63-related ectodermal dysplasia syndrome that may include hypodontia, clefting, skin and hair abnormalities, and occasionally limb malformations.

Rapp-Hodgkin syndrome / TP63-related ect.description: A TP63-associated ectodermal dysplasia characterized by hypodontia or oligodontia, abnormal hair and nails, cleft lip or palate in some individuals, and variable limb abnormalities.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.description: An intermittent supraventricular arrhythmia characterized by episodes of disorganized atrial electrical activity and an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm. The Holter explicitly identifies two episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Frequent premature atrial contractions w.normalized_text: Frequent premature atrial contractions with nonsustained atrial tachycardia
Frequent premature atrial contractions w.description: Premature atrial contractions are early beats arising from the atria. When recurrent consecutive atrial beats occur, they can produce short runs of atrial tachycardia; a high burden may trigger or coexist with atrial fibrillation.

Premature ventricular contractions.description: Premature ventricular contractions are early beats originating in the ventricles. In this recording, the ventricular ectopic burden is low and there are no ventricular tachycardia runs.

Gastric extranodal marginal zone lymphom.normalized_text: Gastric extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (gastric MALT lymphoma)
Gastric extranodal marginal zone lymphom.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the stomach, commonly associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. It can cause erosions, ulcers, enlarged gastric folds, and dense lymphoid infiltration with lymphoepithelial lesions on biopsy.

Gastric adenocarcinoma.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the stomach. It may appear endoscopically as an ulcerated, irregular, infiltrative, or depressed lesion and is confirmed by biopsy showing malignant atypical glands invading the gastric wall.

Helicobacter pylori-associated chronic a.description: Chronic gastric inflammation caused by Helicobacter pylori infection. It can produce erythema, erosions, ulceration, lymphoid follicle formation, and may predispose to both peptic ulcer disease and gastric MALT lymphoma.

Late-presenting left congenital diaphrag.normalized_text: Late-presenting left congenital diaphragmatic hernia (Bochdalek hernia) with intrathoracic stomach
Late-presenting left congenital diaphrag.description: A congenital posterolateral diaphragmatic defect permits abdominal organs, particularly the stomach, to herniate into the thorax. It can present later in childhood or adulthood and mimic a pleural air-fluid collection.

Paraesophageal hiatal hernia with intrat.normalized_text: Paraesophageal hiatal hernia with intrathoracic stomach
Paraesophageal hiatal hernia with intrat.description: A hiatal hernia occurs when the stomach herniates through the esophageal hiatus into the chest. A large paraesophageal hernia may create a retrocardiac or left thoracic air-fluid level and can predispose to gastric volvulus.

Gastric volvulus associated with diaphra.normalized_text: Gastric volvulus associated with diaphragmatic hernia
Gastric volvulus associated with diaphra.description: Gastric volvulus is abnormal twisting of the stomach, often associated with a diaphragmatic defect or paraesophageal hernia. It may result in a distended intrathoracic stomach with an air-fluid level and can become an emergency if strangulation occurs.

Left hydropneumothorax or pyopneumothora.description: Hydropneumothorax is the presence of both air and fluid in the pleural space; when infected it is called pyopneumothorax. It produces a pleural air-fluid level and can compress the lung.

diagnoses.name: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
diagnoses.normalized_text: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver

Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis (IgG4-rel.description: An IgG4-related fibroinflammatory disease of the pancreas characterized by pancreatic enlargement, dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, storiform fibrosis, and increased IgG4-positive plasma cells.

Primary pancreatic lymphoma.description: A lymphoma arising predominantly in the pancreas, often producing a bulky pancreatic mass or diffuse pancreatic enlargement and sometimes resembling pancreatitis or pancreatic carcinoma on imaging.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy, typically an infiltrating duct-forming carcinoma that causes a focal pancreatic mass, biliary obstruction, pancreatic duct dilatation, and metastatic disease.

Chronic pancreatitis.description: Long-standing pancreatic inflammation causing fibrosis and loss of exocrine tissue; it may form an inflammatory pancreatic mass and can overlap radiologically with autoimmune pancreatitis.

Gonorrhea caused by Neisseria gonorrhoea.description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The reported sequence types, mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 mutations, and antimicrobial susceptibility profile are characteristic of gonococcal isolates.

Ceftriaxone-resistant gonorrhea.description: Gonorrhea caused by N. gonorrhoeae with resistance to ceftriaxone, an extended-spectrum cephalosporin commonly used as first-line therapy. This is a major public-health concern because it can limit standard treatment options.

Multidrug-resistant gonococcal infection.description: An infection with N. gonorrhoeae resistant to multiple antimicrobial classes, including cephalosporins, penicillins, and fluoroquinolones. Some isolates also show macrolide resistance.

Giant bullous emphysema (vanishing lung.description: A severe form of bullous emphysema in which very large air-filled bullae replace or compress normal lung tissue, often causing marked unilateral hyperlucency and reduced functional lung volume.

Bullous chronic obstructive pulmonary di.description: COPD with emphysema involves irreversible destruction of alveolar walls and enlargement of air spaces; advanced disease can form bullae and produce lung hyperinflation.

Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associate.description: An inherited deficiency of alpha-1 antitrypsin that can cause early-onset, predominantly lower-lung emphysema and bullous lung destruction, sometimes in nonsmokers.

Bronchiectasis with secondary localized.normalized_text: Bronchiectasis with secondary localized emphysematous/bullous change
Bronchiectasis with secondary localized.description: Bronchiectasis is permanent dilation and distortion of bronchi caused by chronic infection, inflammation, or impaired airway clearance; regional air trapping and destructive lung changes can coexist.

Sporadic Burkitt lymphoma.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly presents with a rapidly growing bulky abdominal or retroperitoneal mass and may involve kidneys, bowel, bone marrow, and other extranodal sites.

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.description: The most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults, often presenting with nodal or extranodal masses, including abdominal, retroperitoneal, renal, or gastrointestinal disease.

B-lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia.description: An aggressive precursor B-cell malignancy composed of lymphoblasts that can form extranodal or abdominal masses and may infiltrate kidneys and bone marrow.

Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa.description: A necrotizing vasculitis affecting small- to medium-sized arteries in the skin, often producing livedo reticularis/racemosa, purpura, painful nodules, ulcers, or infarct-like lesions. Biopsy may show inflamed vessel walls with fibrinoid necrosis and luminal thrombosis.

Livedoid vasculopathy.description: A thrombotic occlusive disease of small cutaneous vessels that causes livedo racemosa, purpura, painful ulceration, and eventually white stellate scars known as atrophie blanche. Histology typically shows fibrin thrombi with relatively limited vessel-wall inflammation.

Antiphospholipid syndrome with cutaneous.normalized_text: Antiphospholipid syndrome with cutaneous thrombotic vasculopathy
Antiphospholipid syndrome with cutaneous.description: An autoimmune prothrombotic disorder characterized by arterial, venous, or small-vessel thrombosis; skin findings can include livedo racemosa, purpura, necrosis, and ulcers due to occluded dermal vessels.

Leukocytoclastic vasculitis (cutaneous s.description: An immune-complex-mediated inflammation of small dermal vessels that commonly causes palpable purpura and may be triggered by infection, medications, autoimmune disease, or malignancy. Histology can show vessel-wall injury, fibrinoid necrosis, and inflammatory cell infiltration.

Classic homocystinuria due to cystathion.normalized_text: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
Classic homocystinuria due to cystathion.description: An inherited disorder of transsulfuration causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It commonly produces ectopia lentis, marfanoid skeletal features, osteoporosis, and increased thromboembolic risk.

Marfan syndrome.description: A connective-tissue disorder, usually caused by pathogenic variants in FBN1, characterized by tall marfanoid habitus, pectus deformity, skeletal changes, and ectopia lentis; cardiovascular aortic disease is an important associated feature.

Remethylation defect causing homocystinu.normalized_text: Remethylation defect causing homocystinuria, such as severe methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) deficiency
Remethylation defect causing homocystinu.description: An inherited defect of homocysteine remethylation that causes hyperhomocysteinemia and may lead to neurologic disease and thrombosis. Unlike CBS deficiency, methionine is usually low or low-normal.

Intraventricular neurocysticercosis.description: Central nervous system infection by the larval form of Taenia solium. Cysts may occur in the fourth ventricle or subarachnoid spaces and can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow, causing hydrocephalus.

Racemose (subarachnoid) neurocysticercos.description: A form of neurocysticercosis involving the subarachnoid cisterns or ventricular system, often with larger multilobulated cysts and a greater risk of chronic arachnoiditis and hydrocephalus.

Fourth-ventricular ependymoma.description: A glial tumor arising from ependymal cells, most commonly located in or near the fourth ventricle, where it can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow and cause hydrocephalus.

Tuberculoma or tuberculous meningitis wi.normalized_text: Tuberculoma or tuberculous meningitis with hydrocephalus
Tuberculoma or tuberculous meningitis wi.description: Central nervous system tuberculosis can cause focal granulomas (tuberculomas) or basal meningeal inflammation that obstructs cerebrospinal-fluid circulation and produces hydrocephalus.

Linfosotiocitosis hemofagocítica secunda.description: Un síndrome hiperinflamatorio potencialmente mortal causado por una activación inmunitaria descontrolada, caracterizado por hemofagocitosis, citopenias, hiperferritinemia, hipertrigliceridemia, lesión hepática e inflamación sistémica.

Leishmaniasis visceral con HLH secundari.description: Una infección sistémica causada por parásitos Leishmania, endémica en países mediterráneos, incluyendo España. Comúnmente causa fiebre, hepatosplenomegalia, pancitopenia, hepatitis y puede desencadenar HLH secundaria; los amastigotos pueden identificarse en macrófagos de médula ósea.

Linfo-linfosiocitocitas hemofagocítica a.description: La HLH puede desencadenarse por malignidades hematológicas, especialmente linfoma de células T o células NK. Produce inflamación severa, citopenias, elevación de ferritina, disfunción hepática y hemofagocitosis de médula.

Cervicofacial actinomycosis with osteomy.description: A chronic invasive bacterial infection, usually caused by Actinomyces species, that can follow dental disease or mucosal trauma and may produce abscesses, draining lesions, necrosis, and destructive osteomyelitis of the mandible or maxilla.

Invasive mucormycosis (rhino-maxillary-o.description: A rapidly destructive opportunistic fungal infection caused by Mucorales fungi. It commonly affects the nasal cavity, palate, maxilla, orbit, and adjacent facial bones, producing tissue necrosis and osteomyelitis, particularly in patients with diabetes or immunosuppression.

Advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma wi.normalized_text: Advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma with mandibular/maxillary invasion
Advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma wi.description: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignant tumor of the oral cavity. Advanced lesions may ulcerate, become infected, and invade the mandible, maxilla, floor of mouth, palate, and adjacent facial structures.

Medication-related osteonecrosis of the.normalized_text: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw or severe chronic jaw osteomyelitis
Medication-related osteonecrosis of the.description: Osteonecrosis of the jaw can occur after antiresorptive or antiangiogenic medication exposure, especially following dental procedures. It presents with exposed necrotic bone, chronic ulceration, secondary infection, sequestra, and progressive mandibular or maxillary destruction.

Cardiac sarcoidosis.description: An inflammatory granulomatous disease in which noncaseating granulomas infiltrate the myocardium, potentially causing conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.

Giant cell myocarditis.description: A rare, often rapidly progressive autoimmune myocarditis characterized by myocardial inflammation, multinucleated giant cells, ventricular arrhythmias, heart block, and heart failure.

Granulomatous myocarditis due to tubercu.description: Myocardial involvement by Mycobacterium tuberculosis is rare and may produce granulomas, conduction defects, arrhythmias, ventricular dysfunction, or pericardial disease.

Cardiac involvement from fungal granulom.normalized_text: Cardiac involvement from fungal granulomatous infection
Cardiac involvement from fungal granulom.description: Disseminated fungal infections can rarely cause granulomatous myocarditis, sometimes with giant cells, conduction defects, and myocardial dysfunction.

Andersen-Tawil syndrome type 1 (KCNJ2-re.normalized_text: Andersen-Tawil syndrome type 1 (KCNJ2-related disorder, long QT syndrome type 7)
Andersen-Tawil syndrome type 1 (KCNJ2-re.description: A rare autosomal-dominant channelopathy caused by pathogenic KCNJ2 variants. It classically causes ventricular arrhythmias, periodic paralysis, and characteristic skeletal/facial features.

Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricula.description: An inherited arrhythmia syndrome characterized by exercise- or emotion-induced bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, usually in patients with structurally normal hearts.

Long QT syndrome due to another ion-chan.normalized_text: Long QT syndrome due to another ion-channel disorder
Long QT syndrome due to another ion-chan.description: A group of inherited cardiac channelopathies causing delayed ventricular repolarization and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias, syncope, and sudden cardiac death.

Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, particula.normalized_text: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, particularly FIP1L1-PDGFRA-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia
Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, particula.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by persistent marked eosinophilia, often with hypercellular bone marrow and eosinophilic infiltration of organs. PDGFRA-rearranged disease can present with very high eosinophil counts and is typically highly responsive to imatinib.
